description: The West End Open House Neighbourhood Festival kicks with a celebratory musical and dance performance in Soho Square Gardens, reflecting the festival theme of "Maybe It's Because I'm a Londoner!", celebrating the many communities that have come to live and work in the West End and and made London their home.

events.name: Maybe It's because I'm a Londoner

factsheet.heading: Maybe It's because I'm a Londoner!
paragraphs:
The West End Open House Neighbourhood Festival is officially opened by the Lord Mayor of Westminster. 
	
A programme of music, dance and performance from the different communities that have come and left their mark on the West End.
Maps, directions and information on the participating Open House venues.

factsheet.heading: Harmony in Diversity - Gideon Reeling - Balancing Act
paragraphs: Can't Be Arts is a collective of over 70 creatives who have pulled together the festival with support from Westminster City Council.  Established in 2024 they developed the first Westminster neighbourhood festival in Soho. Last year they expanded the festival to Chinatown and now the West End.
Harmony in Diversity CIC organises events of music and dance with workshops, shows, holistic therapy workshops and general entertainment to promote good mental and physical wellbeing to all.
Gideon Reeling design & deliver immersive theatre, interactive storytelling & live experiences.  They have created the Soho Shuffle.

Balancing Act Theatre Arts.  They deliver community theatre workshops that use theatre games and the devising process to boost wellbeing and have been working with residents in Westminster for the last 2 years creating several performance pieces. Most recently a devised piece for the festival inspired by the theme ‘Maybe it’s because I’m a Londoner’.
